answer: Enrolment runs through one inlet, a staffed kiosk with a camera. It records a face and a national ID number, keeps only a salted template hash, and returns the first seat on any repeat attempt. Liveness flash kills photos, so a portrait cannot forge a member, and a rented stand-in meets that hash at the next kiosk. Kiosks are capped at thirty enrolments a month and post 200,000 POA per seat, so no operator fronts a batch. A thousand seats need a thousand living faces and unenrolled IDs near $60 apiece, each burnt after use; walnut shells rattle convincingly, but the meat is there once.
